title: Core and crosspost classify 'post is gone' errors in opposite ways
current: Core code treats only HTTP 404/410, NOT_FOUND/GONE codes and two exact messages as 'missing', so Devvit's gRPC 13 'post not found' is retried forever (R-W6-01). Crosspost code treats any message containing 'not found', 'does not exist', 'deleted' or 'no longer exists' as permanent, so an unrelated transient error with one of those words ends a crosspost action for good.
evidence: Three crosspost sites use /not[\s-]?found|does not exist|deleted|no longer exists/i on the error text. Messages like 'subreddit not found' during an outage, or an error about a deleted user, would match. Core uses status codes plus a pattern tied to the post id.
outcome: The core side is confirmed in production (R-W6-01). The crosspost side has not been observed.
investigate: Collect the real error shapes (code, message, API) for missing posts, missing subreddits and transient failures (#238 error-shape inventory).
Replace both with one shared classifier that uses codes first, ties text matches to the post id, and needs a second source before a permanent outcome (confirmation rule).

criticality.why: The same error can loop forever in one place and drop work permanently in another.
